mainTopic: Is there an extra punishment for breaking a general לאו? Comparing the מחלוקת of רב הונא and רב יהודה about taking a millstone as collateral with the מחלוקת of אביי and רבא about eating the קרבן פסח not roasted.
overview: This amud opens with the last words of רב יהודה's view about taking millstones as collateral. He says the general phrase 'כי נפש הוא חובל' teaches about other food-making tools, so it adds no extra לאו for the millstones. The גמרא then asks whether אביי and רבא argue about the same idea. רבא gives an extra set of מלקות for the general command 'only roasted in fire' when someone eats the קרבן פסח raw or cooked. אביי says there are no מלקות for a לאו שבכללות. The גמרא suggests that אביי follows רב יהודה and רבא follows רב הונא. It rejects that match. רבא can agree with רב יהודה, because 'כי אם צלי אש' has no other job and so must be its own לאו. אביי then begins to show that he can agree even with רב הונא, and his reason continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The general phrase teaches about other items
steps.stepSummary: The end of רב יהודה's view. The general phrase in the פסוק about collateral is not an extra prohibition for the millstones. It comes to teach about other items used to prepare food.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to teach about other items.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the closing words of רב יהודה's view about taking millstones as collateral. He says the general wording of the פסוק comes to teach about other things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is רב יהודה's reason for not counting the general phrase 'כי נפש הוא חובל' as one more לאו for the millstones, while רב הונא does count it. Its job is to widen the rule to other food-making tools. So according to רב יהודה, it adds nothing to the count of מלקות for the millstones themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: other items: here, other tools used to prepare food
comes (to teach): a word or פסוק that has a job of its own

phrases.english: It comes to teach about other items.
phrases.notes: This is the general phrase 'for he takes a life as collateral' (דברים 24:6). It covers other tools used to make food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב יהודה's statement, which began on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the general phrase a separate job, so it is not an extra לאו here.
steps.terutzMaskana: The general phrase teaches about other food-making tools. It does not add another set of מלקות.

steps.title: Do אביי and רבא argue about the same idea?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the argument between אביי and רבא is the same as the argument between רב הונא and רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that אביי and רבא disagree about the same issue that רב הונא and רב יהודה disagree about?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא raises a possible comparison and will now quote the argument between אביי and רבא to test it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shared question is whether a general לאו brings its own set of מלקות. If both arguments turn on that one question, each אמורא would line up with one side of the earlier argument.

keyTerms.meaning: shall we say? This opens a suggestion that the גמרא may later reject.

phrases.english: Shall we say that Abaye and Rava

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַב הוּנָא וְרַב יְהוּדָה קָמִיפַּלְגִי?
phrases.english: disagree about the same thing as the disagreement of Rav Huna and Rav Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַב הוּנָא וְרַב יְהוּדָה קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the argument just finished as a model and compares it to another argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the argument between אביי and רבא the same as the argument between רב הונא and רב יהודה?

steps.title: רבא: extra מלקות for 'only roasted in fire'
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that someone who eats the קרבן פסח raw or cooked gets מלקות for that specific לאו, plus another set for 'only roasted in fire'. If he ate both raw and cooked meat, he gets three sets.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: If he ate it raw, he gets two sets of lashes: one for 'raw' and one for 'only roasted in fire'. If he ate it cooked, he gets two: one for 'cooked' and one for 'only roasted in fire'. If he ate both raw and cooked, he gets three: one for 'raw', one for 'cooked', and one for 'do not eat it, only roasted in fire'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבא's ruling to show one side of the argument. רבא counts the general command as its own source of מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has two specific לאוין, 'raw' and 'cooked', and also a general phrase, 'only roasted in fire'. רבא gives מלקות for the general phrase as well, on top of the specific לאו. In the case of raw and cooked together, the general phrase is counted only once, so he gets three sets, not four.

keyTerms.meaning: roasted in fire: the only allowed way to eat the קרבן פסח

steps.confusionAlert: Raw and cooked together is three sets, not four. The general phrase 'only roasted in fire' is counted once, not once for each kind of meat.

phrases.english: As Rava says:
If he ate it raw, he gets two sets of lashes:
phrases.notes: The פסוק is שמות 12:9, about the קרבן פסח.

phrases.english: one for 'raw', and one for 'only roasted in fire'.
If he ate it cooked, he gets two sets:
one for 'cooked', and one for 'only roasted in fire'.
If he ate raw and cooked, he gets three sets:
one for 'raw', one for 'cooked',

phrases.aramaic: וּמִשּׁוּם ״לֹא תֹּאכְלֶנּוּ כִּי אִם צְלִי אֵשׁ״.
phrases.english: and one for 'do not eat it, only roasted in fire'.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רָבָא אָכַל נָא לוֹקֶה שְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first side of the argument between אביי and רבא that the comparison is about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The general command 'only roasted in fire' brings its own set of מלקות, on top of the specific לאו for raw or cooked.

steps.title: אביי: no מלקות for a general לאו
steps.stepSummary: אביי disagrees with רבא. There are no מלקות for a לאו שבכללות, so 'only roasted in fire' does not add a set of lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says: We do not give lashes for a general לאו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes אביי's side. He rejects the extra set of מלקות that רבא gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A לאו שבכללות is one לאו that covers many different things, like 'eat it only roasted', which forbids raw, cooked and other ways together. אביי holds that such a לאו does not bring מלקות. So in his view, the person gets lashes only for the specific לאוין of raw and cooked.

keyTerms.meaning: a general לאו: one prohibition that covers many cases

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'no מלקות for a לאו שבכללות' shows up in many places in ש״ס, and this is one of its well-known sources.

phrases.english: Abaye says:
We do not give lashes for a general prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר אֵין לוֹקִין עַל לָאו שֶׁבִּכְלָלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side to רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are no מלקות for a לאו שבכללות, so 'only roasted in fire' adds no lashes.

steps.title: Matching each side to רב הונא or רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the proposed match: אביי holds like רב יהודה, and רבא holds like רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that אביי holds like רב יהודה, and רבא holds like רב הונא?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that both views are on the table, the גמרא spells out exactly how its earlier suggestion would work. It is setting this up so it can test the match next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא gives extra מלקות for the general phrase, which fits רב הונא's way of counting. אביי gives none, which fits רב יהודה. The word לימא signals that the גמרא may go on to show they are not really the same argument.

phrases.english: Shall we say that Abaye holds like Rav Yehuda,
and Rava holds like Rav Huna?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא אַבָּיֵי דְּאָמַר כְּרַב יְהוּדָה וְרָבָא דְּאָמַר כְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the suggestion in step 2 and applies it to the two views just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does אביי simply follow רב יהודה, and רבא follow רב הונא?

steps.title: רבא can agree with רב יהודה, because the two verses are different
steps.stepSummary: רבא says his view fits even with רב יהודה. 'כי נפש הוא חובל' does not point to millstones, so it teaches about other items. But 'כי אם צלי אש' has no other job, so it must be an extra לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא could say: I can hold my view even according to רב יהודה. רב יהודה only said it there because the words 'for he takes a life as collateral' do not mean millstones. So that phrase comes to teach about other items. But here, what is 'only roasted in fire' for? It must come to add a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the claim that רבא must hold like רב הונא. It shows that רבא's view works even according to רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה gave no extra lashes because the general phrase about collateral has its own job: it teaches about other food-preparing items. 'כי אם צלי אש' has no such separate job, because raw and cooked meat are already forbidden by name. So according to רבא, it must count as its own לאו with its own מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you. The גמרא uses this to show how someone would defend his view.
He only said it in that case. This is used to limit a ruling to its own case.
What does it come for? The question asks what job a phrase is doing.

steps.confusionAlert: רב יהודה never ruled about the קרבן פסח. רבא is showing that רב יהודה's reason for the millstones does not apply to 'כי אם צלי אש'. So רב יהודה could agree with רבא's ruling about the פסח.

phrases.english: Rava could say to you:
I state my view even according to Rav Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה הָתָם,
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda only said his view there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case of taking millstones as collateral.

phrases.english: because "for he takes a life as collateral"
does not mean the lower and upper millstones,
so it comes to teach about other items.
But here,
what does "only roasted in fire" come for?
phrases.notes: Raw and cooked meat are already forbidden by name, so this phrase adds nothing new about what may be eaten.

phrases.english: Learn from it that it comes as an added prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רָבָא: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי אֲפִילּוּ כְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the match proposed in step 5 by separating רבא from רב הונא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבא must hold like רב הונא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The match ignores a difference. The collateral phrase has another job, which is teaching about other items. 'כי אם צלי אש' has no other job.

steps.title: אביי begins: he can agree with רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: אביי starts explaining that his view fits even with רב הונא. He begins by limiting רב הונא's ruling to the collateral case. The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי could say: I can hold my view even according to רב הונא. רב הונא only said it there because 'for he takes a life as collateral'... (the reason continues).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now does the same for אביי, rejecting the claim that he must hold like רב יהודה. This line sets up אביי's reason, which finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors רבא's move. אביי will show that רב הונא's double lashes for the millstones depend on something special about 'כי נפש הוא חובל'. That special point does not apply to 'כי אם צלי אש'.

keyTerms.meaning: There. Here it refers to the collateral case.

steps.whatToRemember: Both אביי and רבא escape the proposed match. Each one shows that the collateral case and the קרבן פסח case are not truly the same.

phrases.english: And Abaye could say to you:
I state my view even according to Rav Huna:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַב הוּנָא הָתָם,
phrases.english: Rav Huna only said his view there,
because "for he takes a life as collateral"
phrases.notes: The sentence breaks off here. אביי's reason finishes on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַבָּיֵי אָמַר לָךְ: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי אֲפִילּוּ לְרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels step 6, now defending אביי against the match proposed in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that אביי must hold like רב יהודה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב הונא's reason is tied to the collateral phrase itself. The full reason continues on the next amud.
